subject: viperfish
title: This Deep-Sea Fish Has Teeth Too Long to Fit Inside Its Own Mouth

scenes.text: This deep-sea fish has teeth too long for its own mouth.
The viperfish is only about a foot long, but its fangs are so big they stick out even when its jaws are shut.
By day it waits in the dark, hundreds of meters down. At night it swims up toward the surface to hunt.
A long spine on its back carries a glowing lure that dangles in front of its mouth.
When a fish swims in to look, the viperfish lunges, and those fangs lock together like a cage.
Teeth too big for the mouth sounds like a design flaw. In the dark, it's the trap.

description:
This deep-sea fish has teeth too long for its own mouth.
The viperfish is only about a foot long, but its fangs stay outside its mouth even when closed. It lives in the dark deep ocean by day and rises toward the surface at night, dangling a glowing lure from its back to draw in prey, then snapping its fangs together like a cage.
Would you swim toward that light?
